title: A finite type algebra is locally quasi-finite over a polynomial algebra in its fibre dimension
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], let $\mathfrak q\subset S$ be prime, and let $\mathfrak p\subset R$ be its inverse image. Write $F=S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ for the fibre ring [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and $\mathfrak Q=\ker(F\to\kappa(\mathfrak q))$ for the corresponding prime. Suppose the Krull dimension of $\operatorname{Spec}F$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] at $\mathfrak Q$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] is an integer $n\ge0$. Then there are $g\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$ and an $R$-algebra homomorphism $R[t_1,\dots,t_n]\to S_g$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-ring-localization-away] which is quasi-finite: it is of finite type and quasi-finite at every prime of $S_g$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime].

proof.text: The private helper exists_away_fibre_dimension_eq puts p=q cap R, F=kappa(p) tensor_R S, and Q=preimageHomeomorphFiber(q). The inverse fibre homeomorphism followed by subtype inclusion identifies Spec F with an embedded subspace of Spec S (Mathlib PrimeSpectrum.preimageHomeomorphFiber). The well order on WithBot ENat makes the infimum of dimensions of open neighbourhoods attained, using ciInf_mem. Write the minimizing neighbourhood as the inverse image of an open V of Spec S under this embedding. Choose a basic open D(g0) in V containing q. Its inverse image is D(1 tensor g0), which has dimension at most the minimizing neighbourhood by subspace monotonicity and at least dim_Q Spec F by the defining infimum. The base-change equivalence IsLocalization.Away.tensorProductEquivTMulRight and the localization spectrum homeomorphism then give dim Spec(kappa(p) tensor_R S_g0)=n. The range theorem localization_away_comap_range supplies q0 in Spec S_g0 contracting to q.

proof.text: The private helper exists_polynomial_isQuasiFiniteAtPrime_of_fibre_dimension applies exists_finite_inj_algHom_mvPolynomial_of_ringKrullDim_eq to the nonzero finite-type fibre F=kappa(p) tensor_R S_g0. Its nontriviality follows from the point Q. For each normalized variable image y_i, Ideal.Fiber.exists_smul_eq_one_tmul gives u_i not in p and s_i in S_g0 with u_i*y_i=1 tensor s_i. Define units v_i in kappa(p) from these u_i. The aeval map X_i -> C(v_i)*X_i has inverse X_i -> C(v_i inverse)*X_i, as checked with MvPolynomial.algHom_ext. Composing the finite normalization map with this automorphism remains finite and sends X_i to 1 tensor s_i. The real coordinate map is f0=aeval s. The original finite generators give finite type over the polynomial algebra via FiniteType.of_restrictScalars_finiteType.

proof.text: Let A=R[t_1,...,t_n] and Ak=kappa(p) tensor_R A. MvPolynomial.algebraTensorAlgEquiv identifies Ak with kappa(p)[t_1,...,t_n]. Composing this equivalence with the rescaled finite normalization makes F finite over Ak. Equality of the two maps A -> F is proved on coefficients and variables with MvPolynomial.ringHom_ext; it gives a commuting square on spectra. Both vertical maps Spec F -> Spec S_g0 and Spec Ak -> Spec A are embeddings furnished by the fibre homeomorphisms. Every prime in the fibre of Spec S_g0 -> Spec A through q0 lies over p in Spec R, hence lifts to Spec F. The private topological lemma isOpen_singleton_fiber_of_embedding therefore identifies this whole fibre with the fibre upstairs: restrict the embedding to the inverse-image fibre and prove its surjectivity using the covering condition; the resulting homeomorphism transports open singletons. The finite Ak-algebra F is quasi-finite by Mathlib, so quasiFiniteAt_iff_isOpen_singleton_fiber makes the upstairs singleton open. This yields IsQuasiFiniteAtPrime A S_g0 q0, without the original scheme-level zero-dimensional Artinian lemma.

proof.text: The private equivalence isQuasiFiniteAtPrime_iff_quasiFiniteAt transports the defining open singleton across preimageHomeomorphFiber and applies Mathlib quasiFiniteAt_iff_isOpen_singleton_fiber. Use the resulting QuasiFiniteAt A q0 directly in Mathlib QuasiFiniteAt.exists_fg_and_exists_notMem_and_awayMap_bijective (ZariskisMainTheorem): it supplies a finite A-subalgebra Sprime and r in Sprime outside q0, with bijective awayMap from Sprime_r to (S_g0)_r. Module finiteness gives QuasiFinite A Sprime, preserved by localization and the surjective awayMap. Thus the further localization T is quasi-finite at every prime. This uses the already proved Mathlib finite-subalgebra theorem directly instead of the project openness theorem.

proof.text: Put h=r in S_g0 and b=(IsLocalization.Away.sec g0 h).1. Mathlib associated_sec_fst says that the image of b is associated to h. If b were in q, its image would be in q0 and Ideal.mem_iff_of_associated would put h in q0, a contradiction. Hence g=g0*b avoids q. IsLocalization.Away.mul_of_associated makes T a localization of S away from g. IsLocalization.algEquiv gives T equiv S_g. Compose f0 with the canonical S_g0 -> T and this equivalence, restricted to R, to obtain the requested R-algebra map f. FiniteType.of_restrictScalars_finiteType proves finite type over A. Regard the equivalence as an A-algebra equivalence using the constructed f; for each prime qprime of S_g, contract it to T and transport QuasiFiniteAt using of_surjectiveOnStalks and the surjectivity of the equivalence. Finally isQuasiFiniteAtPrime_iff_quasiFiniteAt gives the requested isolated-fibre-point property. All definitions are genuine constructions; the proof only eliminates existential witnesses in a theorem.
